title: agent-atlas Gate manifest (controls layer)
description: A declarative, versioned contract for one GATE — a control over a consequential transition. Gates are a CONTROLS LAYER, distinct from the seven component kinds (which describe the system); a gate governs a transition of the system. A gate binds: the transition it guards, a PLUGGABLE deterministic reasoner (the proof engine — NEVER an LLM), the rules + fact schema it proves against (instance-specific), and a mode. The proof spine lives here. No LLM may sit in a gate's path: that is the safety invariant that makes the proof authoritative.

transition.description: The consequential transition this gate guards, e.g. 'validate->package' (G-PROMOTE) or 'act' (G-ACT). Free-form but should name the from->to stages or the stage where the action fires.

reasoner.description: The PLUGGABLE deterministic proving engine behind evaluate(facts,rules)->verdict+violations. ALWAYS deterministic (a logic/constraint solver), NEVER an LLM — pinning a proof to an LLM is a category error that turns a proof into a plausible guess.

engine.description: The reasoner family, e.g. 'asp' (Answer Set Programming) or 'smt'. Pluggable per the framework's reasoner interface.

version.description: Pinned implementation version for reproducibility, e.g. '5.8.0'.

rules_ref.description: INSTANCE-specific reference (path/id) to the declared rules this gate proves against (e.g. an ASP program). The rules are the control; the engine is plumbing. [I]

fact_schema.description: INSTANCE-specific reference (path/id) to the typed fact schema the proposal is grounded into before proving. [I]

mode.description: 'shadow' attests 'would have done X' without effect; 'live' executes on PERMITTED. New gates default to shadow.

governance.description: Regime-neutral controls (NIST AI RMF). A gate is itself a governed control surface.
